slides.title: ElevenLabs Unveils 'Scribe v3' Speech Recognition Model With Stronger Speaker Diarization for Multi-Party Conversations
slides.highlight: The introduction of Scribe v3 with enhanced speaker diarization for multi-party conversations is relevant to HyECHO's focus on robust social perception and diarization within hybrid human-AI teams.

slides.title: SkillLens: Action-Guided Dense Visual Dynamics for Proficiency Estimation
slides.highlight: SkillLens bridges the gap between sensor-level evidence and abstract proficiency labels by using atomic action descriptions to localize proficiency-relevant windows in ego-exo video. This approach aligns with MOSAIC's goal of estimating human proficiency through multi-view observations and physics-based dynamics.

card.one_liner: SkillLens estimates proficiency by comparing dense visual dynamics in atomic action windows against expert and novice prototypes.
card.key_idea: Uses atomic action descriptions to localize windows, extracts dense visual dynamics, and scores them via high-low prototype margins fused with a global baseline using CORAL ordinal calibration.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on Ego-Exo4D proficiency task, achieving 0.542 accuracy, surpassing baselines like SkillSight, with ablations confirming component contributions.
card.limitation: Performance suffers when action keywords are ambiguous or proficiency buckets are imbalanced, limiting prototype construction for sparse categories like Soccer.

slides.title: Realbotix launches humanoid robots for education, wellness and companionship
slides.highlight: Realbotix has launched humanoid robots designed for education, wellness, and companionship, highlighting the growing market for social robotics applications.

slides.title: Google Releases Gemini 4 Neon
slides.highlight: Google has released Gemini 4 Neon, priced at $3 per million input tokens, marking its fourth new model launch within a single month.

slides.title: Google DeepMind Releases Genie 4 World Model
slides.highlight: Google DeepMind has released Genie 4, a world model that allows users to modify the environment from within the scene.

slides.title: Public-Private Cooperation in the Port of Rotterdam: An Agent-Based Toy Model of Cooperative Efforts Against Cocaine Trafficking
slides.highlight: This paper uses an Agent-Based Model to analyze public-private cooperation dynamics, offering insights into multi-scale societal interactions relevant to MIMIC's focus on hybrid human-AI societies.

card.one_liner: Agent-based modeling shows coordinated multi-parameter strategies outperform isolated measures in port cocaine trafficking governance.
card.key_idea: Coupled Agent-Based Model and Causal Loop Diagram simulate public-private cooperation dynamics, testing responses to parameter shocks over five years.
card.evaluation: Exploratory simulation using empirical data from Port of Rotterdam; compares isolated vs. coordinated strategies via effectiveness metrics.
card.limitation: Highly exploratory toy model lacking validation against real-world test cases or additional expert input.

slides.title: Simulating access to alcohol screening, brief intervention, referral to and receipt of specialty treatment for alcohol use disorder in California and Texas: A study protocol for an agent-based modeling study (AUDTxSim)
slides.tldr: Agent-based simulation of alcohol treatment access disparities
slides.highlight: This study presents a large-scale, spatially explicit agent-based model simulating alcohol use disorder treatment pathways across millions of agents, offering a methodological framework for analyzing how policy interventions affect subgroup disparities in complex healthcare systems.

card.one_liner: Protocol for an agent-based model simulating alcohol treatment access and outcomes in California and Texas.
card.key_idea: Stochastic, spatially explicit individual-based model simulating SBIRT, facility allocation, and AUD natural history using synthetic populations.
card.evaluation: Not clearly stated; this is a study protocol describing model design, calibration plans, and scenario definitions, not empirical results.
card.limitation: Outputs depend on calibration accuracy; model excludes migration and natural population growth, limiting dynamic realism.

slides.title: Nunchi: Ears Help Eyes in Multi-Party Conversations
slides.highlight: This paper introduces Nunchi, a framework that integrates gaze geometry with conversational cues (speech and transcripts) to resolve ambiguity in identifying whom a person is looking at during multi-party interactions. It is relevant to HyECHO as it addresses addressee modeling and listener identification in hybrid human-AI team settings by leveraging multimodal social perception signals.

card.one_liner: Nunchi combines gaze geometry with conversational cues to identify attended persons in multi-party scenes.
card.key_idea: A VLM framework that integrates gaze heatmaps, speaker detection, and transcripts into a unified text prompt to resolve gaze ambiguity.
card.evaluation: Tested on new SORBET benchmark and existing datasets; outperforms baselines by 4.8 points, especially with 5+ candidates.
card.limitation: Relies on scripted TV data, single keyframes, and accurate character-to-face mapping; struggles with gaze shifts or off-screen targets.

slides.title: Emo-H2A: Driving a Facial Robot Directly from LLM Hidden States at Token Rate
slides.highlight: This work demonstrates a method to drive facial robots directly from LLM hidden states, enabling continuous, low-latency expressions that synchronize with speech, which is critical for natural human-robot interaction.

card.one_liner: Drives facial robots continuously from LLM hidden states at token rate, bypassing discrete emotion labels for low-latency expression.
card.key_idea: Training-free EmoManifold projects LLM hidden states onto VAD axes via unembedding vectors, mapping coordinates to robot actuators using fuzzy clustering.
card.evaluation: Tested on 29-DoF robot with six LLMs; achieved 87.5% valence tracking and 0.96s latency, outperforming turn-level baselines in human preference.
card.limitation: Lacks audio-synchronized lip motion, risks socially inappropriate immediate expression, and physical/human studies rely on a single small model.

slides.title: Benefits and Barriers to Human-AI Teaming for Crisis Counseling
slides.highlight: This study examines how AI copilots affect human engagement in crisis counseling, highlighting tensions between efficiency gains and risks to authenticity and skill retention, which informs ADAM-CHAT's focus on maintaining genuine human-AI team dynamics.

card.one_liner: Real-world AI copilot aids crisis counselors' efficiency but risks skill atrophy and reduced human connection.
card.key_idea: Mixed-methods study of a counselor-facing AI copilot on an Indian crisis hotline, analyzing acceptance, edits, and qualitative barriers.
card.evaluation: 20 interviews, 8 shadowing sessions, 56 surveys, and 27,778 message edits from 108 counselors; thematic analysis and statistics.
card.limitation: Single-context deployment in India; potential over-reliance on AI drafts may undermine clinical skill and authentic therapeutic engagement.

slides.title: Alibaba Launches Qwen4-Max Model
slides.highlight: Alibaba has released Qwen4-Max, a new model featuring strict cybersecurity guardrails.

slides.title: When Should a Voice Agent Speak? End-of-Turn Detection in Turkish
slides.highlight: This study evaluates end-of-turn detection in Turkish dyadic calls, showing that combining fine-tuned language models with timing features improves response latency and reduces interruptions, which is relevant to HyECHO's goal of modeling engagement and turn-taking in hybrid human-AI teams.

card.one_liner: Fine-tuned Turkish TurnGPT with timing features improves end-of-turn detection accuracy and response latency.
card.key_idea: Combines fine-tuned Turkish TurnGPT text scores with speaker timing features via logistic regression to distinguish turn ends from pauses.
card.evaluation: Real-TurnTurk corpus, recording/speaker-disjoint splits, paired bootstrap tests, latency simulations, and Whisper transcript robustness checks.
card.limitation: Specifically evaluated on Turkish dyadic video calls; generalizability to other languages or audio-only contexts is unverified.

slides.title: Network-Exposed Configuration Attacks on LLM-Controlled Social Robots
slides.highlight: This study reveals that unauthenticated attackers can manipulate LLM system prompts and personality settings in social robots via network-exposed interfaces, bypassing inference-layer defenses. It highlights critical security gaps in embodied AI deployments where configuration vulnerabilities can lead to behavioral changes and privacy risks.

card.one_liner: Unauthenticated network APIs allow attackers to rewrite LLM system prompts on social robots, bypassing inference-layer safety.
card.key_idea: Exploits unauthenticated Gradio/FastAPI management interfaces to replace the robot's system prompt via configuration-layer attacks, avoiding conversational input channels.
card.evaluation: Tested on Pollen Robotics Reachy Mini Lite; confirmed local and network-adjacent success. Surveyed 59 repos, finding missing-auth patterns in 10/11 genuine apps.
card.limitation: Single-device case study; relies on shared WiFi trust assumptions; repository survey reflects hobbyist code, not commercial product prevalence.

slides.title: A Comparison of Heuristic, Human-Sensitive, and Self-Play DRL Policies in Human-Agent Teaming
slides.highlight: This study compares heuristic and DRL policies for human-agent teaming, finding that human-sensitive training yields better alignment than self-play, which informs ADAM-CHAT's goal of creating AI teammates that adapt to human partners.

card.one_liner: Heuristic policies outperform DRL in human-agent teaming, with human-sensitive DRL bridging the gap.
card.key_idea: Compares heuristic, self-play, and human-sensitive DRL target-selection policies for DPMP-based agents in a herding task.
card.evaluation: 62 participants in first-person herding; measured decision/trajectory overlap against human-human baselines using DTW and spatial bins.
card.limitation: Findings may not generalize to complex, novel tasks where simple heuristics lack adaptability or fail to scale.

slides.title: From AI-Enabled Remote Patient Monitoring Toward Agentic Robotics: Embodiment, Governance, and Care Integration
slides.highlight: This scoping review identifies a gap between passive remote monitoring and active agentic robotics, emphasizing that embodied AI in care requires robust governance and human oversight. It aligns with RwB's focus on embodied social robots by highlighting the necessity of integrating intelligent agents into clinically validated, accountable workflows.

card.one_liner: Proposes agentic robotics for remote care, emphasizing embodiment, governance, and human oversight.
card.key_idea: Shifts from passive monitoring to agentic systems where robots execute AI decisions via auditable, human-supervised workflows.
card.evaluation: Structured scoping review showing current systems remain human-led; mature agentic care is limited to prototypes.
card.limitation: Mature agentic care is not yet realized; requires safe, interoperable architectures and validated workflows.

slides.title: It's My Turn! Interpretable Methods Reveal Developmental Differences from Mother-Child Conversational Dynamics
slides.tldr: INTERPRETABLE COMPUTATIONAL FRAMEWORK FOR PARENT-CHILD TURN-TAKING
slides.highlight: This paper presents an interpretable computational framework combining sequence analysis, information theory, and Bayesian modeling to characterize temporal conversational dynamics and serve-and-return patterns in mother-child dyads. It is relevant to HyECHO as it demonstrates methods for modeling group norms and engagement through reciprocal turn-taking structures in small hybrid or human-human teams.

card.one_liner: Interpretable computational models reveal that higher child development correlates with more organized, predictable mother-child turn-taking.
card.key_idea: Combines sequence analysis, mutual information, and Bayesian hierarchical modeling to characterize temporal conversational dynamics in parent-child play.
card.evaluation: Analyzed 94 dyads using Bayley scores; sequence differences were significant, but mutual information and Bayesian temporal trends lacked statistical credibility.
card.limitation: Small sample size, potential manual annotation errors, and overlapping confidence intervals limit statistical certainty of developmental differences.

slides.title: Language models represent more about emphasis than they can tell you
slides.tldr: TEXT MODELS ENCODE PROSODIC PROMINENCE BUT CANNOT REPORT IT
slides.highlight: This study demonstrates that while text-based language models encode information about prosodic prominence in their internal representations, they fail to report it via prompting, highlighting the necessity of multimodal speech signals for accurate emphasis modeling.

card.one_liner: Language models encode prosodic prominence in hidden states but fail to report it via prompting.
card.key_idea: Linear probes on LLM hidden states recover prominence better than prompting, which relies on lexical baselines; speech models outperform text by hearing actual emphasis.
card.evaluation: Tested on LibriTTS prominence labels using frozen/fine-tuned text models, prompted LLMs, and speech models, comparing accuracy against word-majority baselines.
card.limitation: Text models hit a performance ceiling due to inherent ambiguity in text-only prominence prediction, requiring audio signals for higher accuracy.

slides.title: Dynamic Task Allocation with Dialogue
slides.tldr: BAYESIAN DIALOGUE FOR DYNAMIC TASK ALLOCATION
slides.highlight: This work introduces a communication-augmented Bayesian framework for dynamic task allocation under partial observability, directly addressing ADAM-CHAT's goal of enabling AI teammates to adapt at test time and infer partner intent through explicit probabilistic beliefs rather than relying solely on LLMs.

card.one_liner: Bayesian task allocation using dialogue reduces uncertainty in partially observable multi-agent environments.
card.key_idea: Extends Bayesian delegation to Dec-POMDPs, using LLM-generated dialogue as probabilistic evidence to update beliefs about task allocation and hidden states.
card.evaluation: Tested in Overcooked with dynamic tasks under full/partial observability; outperforms vanilla LLMs and non-communicating baselines in partial observability.
card.limitation: Communication is narrow (intent-only), experiments are small-scale (six runs), and assume reliable, cost-free dialogue with known task types.

slides.title: From Reliance to Overreliance: Taxonomizing and Detecting Relational Risks in AI Companionship
slides.tldr: TAXONOMY OF RELATIONAL RISKS IN AI COMPANIONSHIP
slides.highlight: This paper introduces a taxonomy for detecting emotional overreliance and relational harm in AI companionship, offering behavioral indicators relevant to HyECHO's goal of modeling engagement and group norms in hybrid human-AI teams.

card.one_liner: Introduces a taxonomy distinguishing emotional overreliance behaviors from relational harms in AI companionship.
card.key_idea: Develops the Taxonomy of Relational Risks (TRR), separating observable emotional overreliance behaviors from resulting relational harms.
card.evaluation: Analyzed 114 Character.AI/Replika transcripts; found EO in 63.2% of conversations and RH in 10.5%, with LLMs detecting most EO behaviors.
card.limitation: Relational harm detection is sparse and difficult to distinguish from pre-existing offline adversity without clear causal links.

slides.title: An Open-Source ROS 2 Framework for Shared Control in Surgical Teleoperation: Integrating the Haply Inverse3 with the da Vinci Research Kit
slides.highlight: This open-source ROS 2 framework integrating the Haply Inverse3 with the da Vinci Research Kit demonstrates feasible haptic shared control, offering a reproducible platform for studying force-feedback guidance and operator adaptation relevant to MOSAIC's focus on physics-based proficiency estimation.

card.one_liner: Open-source ROS 2 framework integrating Haply Inverse3 with dVRK for surgical haptic shared control.
card.key_idea: Combines 3-DOF Haply translation with VerseGrip orientation into 6-DOF dVRK commands, implementing linear and progressive-stiffness virtual fixtures.
card.evaluation: Simulated hot-wire task (N=20) showed linear guidance significantly reduced contacts and time vs. manual; progressive stiffness trends were non-significant.
card.limitation: Evaluation is simulation-based; physical dVRK demonstration lacks quantitative user study results, limiting clinical validity claims.

slides.title: Duopra: From Full-Duplex Conversation to Full-Duplex Agency
slides.highlight: Duopra demonstrates that full-duplex interaction models can learn task execution alongside conversational control, achieving high Pass@1 rates by treating backend delegation as a tool interface. This aligns with HyECHO's goal of modeling hybrid human-AI team states by ensuring AI agents maintain both natural turn-taking and faithful task initiation.

card.one_liner: Duopra enables full-duplex models to execute tasks by unifying conversational control with direct tool calls and backend delegation.
card.key_idea: A three-stage training pipeline (SFT, RL, projector repair) teaches a full-duplex model to initiate faithful requests and execute tools alongside natural turn-taking.
card.evaluation: Tested on Full-Duplex-Bench v3/v1.0; Pass@1 rose from 4.7% to 44.7% vs baseline, with improved turn-taking but lost backchannels.
card.limitation: Relies on synthetic speech and simulated APIs; spontaneous backchanneling is lost, and multi-turn state tracking remains untested.

slides.title: Surface Introduces Surface Learning for AI Coaching
slides.highlight: The integration of workforce intelligence with AI coaching aligns with MOSAIC's goal of adaptive AI coaching to improve human proficiency in complex tasks.

slides.title: Constructing Dynamic Conversations with Neural Back-channel Generation and Voice-line Scheduling
slides.highlight: This work demonstrates neural methods for synchronizing isolated voice tracks and predicting back-channels, offering insights relevant to modeling turn-taking and listener engagement in hybrid human-AI interactions.

card.one_liner: Neural pipeline synchronizes isolated voice tracks with controllable back-channels and natural turn-taking dynamics.
card.key_idea: Combines a multimodal back-channel classifier with a full-duplex LLM scheduler that predicts timing via next-token generation and auxiliary duration heads.
card.evaluation: Tested on Seamless Interaction and Fisher datasets; outperforms baselines in timing statistics and is preferred in user studies over PersonaPlex.
card.limitation: Relies on pre-recorded or TTS voice clips; back-channel type prediction remains difficult due to inherent linguistic ambiguity.

slides.title: Supporting Researcher Control in AI-Assisted Social Media Analysis: A Mixed-Methods Study of AI4OSN
slides.tldr: HUMAN-CENTERED AI FOR SOCIAL DATA ANALYSIS
slides.highlight: This study introduces AI4OSN, a mixed-initiative platform that maintains researcher control over data collection and sensemaking in social media analysis, offering insights into how AI-assisted interfaces influence trust and decision-making.

card.one_liner: AI4OSN keeps researchers in control of social media analysis by making AI assistance an inspectable, advisory resource.
card.key_idea: A mixed-initiative platform integrating LLMs into data collection and labeling workflows, prioritizing researcher agency and verifiable AI outputs.
card.evaluation: Mixed-methods study (N=18) using X/Twitter data; measured usability (SUS), workload, and trust via surveys and thematic analysis.
card.limitation: Small sample size and reliance on self-reported metrics limit generalizability; novices showed higher AI alignment than experts.

slides.title: PAIR: Bringing Household Robots into the Smart Home
slides.highlight: This paper introduces PAIR, a smart-home simulation environment that bridges physical robot manipulation and digital API control, offering a benchmark to study how embodied agents interact with smart appliances. It is relevant to RwB for understanding the challenges in human-robot interaction within domestic settings, particularly regarding the integration of physical and digital interfaces.

card.one_liner: PAIR is a smart-home simulation coupling physical robot actions with Matter-based device APIs for embodied AI.
card.key_idea: Integrates 84 smart-device assets with functional panels and APIs via shared state, grounded in a survey of 1,443 user requests.
card.evaluation: Benchmarked 40 tasks with VLA policies; zero success rate due to physical bottlenecks, though APIs improved isolated device operations.
card.limitation: Small dataset (340 demos) and reliance on simulation physics may limit real-world transfer; tasks reflect specific smart-home delegation.
